title: Exact small-etale restriction and comparison calculus for fibred big-etale modules
statement: Work in the universes and small-skeleton convention of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $p:\mathcal C\to\mathit{Sch}/S$ a category fibred in groupoids [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Give $\mathcal C$ the big etale topology: objects and arrows are those of $\mathcal C$, and coverings lie over jointly surjective etale scheme families [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Put $\mathcal O_{\mathcal C}(z)=\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ for $z$ over $U$, with the usual pullback of regular functions on arrows. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For $z$ over $U$, define $R_zF$ on $U_{\mathrm{et}}$ by $(R_zF)(v:V\to U)=F(v^*z)$, with restrictions from cartesian lifts. This defines an exact functor $R_z:\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{et}},\mathcal O_{\mathcal C})\to\operatorname{Mod}(U_{\mathrm{et}},\mathcal O_U)$. In particular it preserves kernels, cokernels and short exact sequences. For each arrow $a:z\to z'$ over $u:U\to U'$, restriction induces a natural comparison $c_{a,F}:u_{\mathrm{et}}^*R_{z'}F\to R_zF$, where $u_{\mathrm{et}}^*$ is tensor pullback of modules on the ringed small etale topoi [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], explicitly $u_{\mathrm{et}}^*M=\mathcal O_U\otimes_{u_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}\mathcal O_{U'}}u_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}M$. These comparisons are natural in $F$, are the identity for identity arrows, and satisfy $c_{b\circ a,F}=c_{a,F}\circ u_{\mathrm{et}}^*(c_{b,F})$ for composable arrows $a$ over $u$ and $b$ over $v$, under the canonical tensor-pullback identification $(v\circ u)_{\mathrm{et}}^*\simeq u_{\mathrm{et}}^*v_{\mathrm{et}}^*$. If $u$ is etale, $c_{a,F}$ is an isomorphism, and $u_{\mathrm{et}}^*$ is restriction to the slice $U'_{\mathrm{et}}/U\simeq U_{\mathrm{et}}$. For every functor $h:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$ over $\mathit{Sch}/S$, with $\mathcal D$ also fibred in groupoids and endowed with the same big etale topology and structure sheaf, precomposition $h^*F(y)=F(h(y))$ is a module sheaf. There are canonical identifications $R_y(h^*F)\simeq R_{h(y)}F$ carrying $c_{a,h^*F}$ to $c_{h(a),F}$ for every arrow $a$ of $\mathcal D$. No quasi-coherence, algebraicity or flatness assumption is imposed.

source.place: Tags 075D (lemma-comparison), (1)--(4), and 06WE (equation-functoriality-sheaves-modules), including the module comparison formula equation-comparison-modules; 06TS (lemma-functoriality-sheaves) for precomposition; 06W9 (lemma-localizing-structure-sheaf) for ringed restriction. Exact small-etale restriction is used explicitly in the proof of 06WM (lemma-lqc-colimits), (2)--(3).

proof.text: The ring presheaves are sheaves, as the module-sheaf categories require: by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme] with $R$ the polynomial ring over $\mathbf Z$ in one variable $t$, $T\mapsto\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$ is, as a presheaf of sets, $T\mapsto\operatorname{Mor}(T,\operatorname{Spec}R)$ (a morphism corresponds to the image of $t$), with pullback of regular functions corresponding to composition. A covering of $U_{\mathrm{et}}$ is an fpqc covering [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-finer-than-etale], so [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent] gives the sheaf condition of $\mathcal O_U$ on $U_{\mathrm{et}}$; ring operations are sectionwise. A covering $\{z_i\to z\}$ of $\mathcal C_{\mathrm{et}}$ lies over a covering $\{U_i\to U\}$ of $U_{\mathrm{et}}$, and its pairwise fibre products lie over $U_i\times_UU_j$ by [lem-sfb-cartesian-lift-pullback-square], so the sheaf condition of $\mathcal O_{\mathcal C}$ on it is that of $\mathcal O_U$. Choose cartesian lifts $z_V\to z$ for every $V\to U$. The lifting uniqueness in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids] supplies the arrow $z_W\to z_V$ over each $W\to V$; its identity and composition laws follow because the two candidate composites have the same composite to $z$. Thus $V\mapsto F(z_V)$ is a presheaf, independently of these choices up to their unique isomorphisms. For a covering $\{V_i\to V\}$ in $U_{\mathrm{et}}$, the lifted arrows cover $z_V$ by definition of the inherited topology. Their pairwise pullbacks are lifts of $V_i\times_VV_j$ by [lem-sfb-cartesian-lift-pullback-square]. The sheaf equalizer diagram for $F$ on this cover is exactly that for $R_zF$. Its scalar ring at $V$ is $\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$, and the semilinearity axiom of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] supplies its module restrictions. A module map is restricted componentwise, preserving identities, composition and addition. This constructs $R_z$.

source.place: Definition-pullback, preceding Tag 075D; ringed restriction Tag 06W9; structure sheaf: section-structure-sheaf (sheaf property of p^{-1}O)

proof.text: Kernels are sectionwise by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], so $R_z\ker(f)=\ker(R_zf)$. If $f:F\to G$ is epic, [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful](1) and [lem-weil-pbc-site-abelian-sheaf-epi-locally-surjective] imply that any $s\in G(z_V)$ lifts over a covering $\{w_i\to z_V\}$ of the fibred site. Each $w_i$ lies over a scheme $W_i$ etale over $V$, hence over $U$, and is uniquely isomorphic over $z_V$ to the chosen lift $z_{W_i}$. The $W_i$ jointly cover $V$. These lifts therefore prove local surjectivity of $R_zf$, so it is epic by the same criterion and the faithful exact forgetful functor (which reflects zero cokernels). Thus $R_z$ preserves kernels and epimorphisms. A short exact sequence remains short exact: its first term is the kernel of the second map, whose restriction is epic. For a general $f:F\to G$, apply this to $0\to\ker(f)\to F\to\operatorname{im}(f)\to0$ and $0\to\operatorname{im}(f)\to G\to\operatorname{coker}(f)\to0$; the first identifies the restricted image and the second identifies the restricted cokernel. No surjectivity on unlocalized sections is asserted.

For $u:U\to U'$, put $B_u(V)=U\times_{U'}V$ on the small etale sites. It preserves finite limits by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits] and coverings by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-continuous]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-site-inverse-image-tensor] to obtain $u^{-1}\dashv u_*$, with $(u_*H)(V)=H(B_uV)$. Pullback of regular functions along $B_uV\to V$ gives a natural ring map $\mathcal O_{U'}\to u_*\mathcal O_U$: it respects restrictions and ring operations because the scheme structural maps do. This is the ringed morphism of [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. Consequently [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction] gives the tensor-formula functor $u^*$ and the natural bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(u^*M,H)=\operatorname{Hom}(M,u_*H)$, where the latter pushforward uses that structural ring map. This fixes the ringed small-etale pullback meant in the statement.

source.place: Tag 075D, comparison-push and comparison-modules; descent.tex Tag 070R(2)

proof.text: Let $a:z\to z'$ lie over $u$. For $V\to U'$ etale, let $z'_V\to z'$ and $z_{B_uV}\to z$ be the chosen lifts. There is a unique arrow $a_V:z_{B_uV}\to z'_V$ over $B_uV\to V$ whose composite to $z'$ is $a\circ(z_{B_uV}\to z)$, by [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Define $d_{a,F,V}=F(a_V):F(z'_V)\to F(z_{B_uV})$. For $t:V_1\to V$, the square of these arrows and the lift restrictions commutes: its two composites to $z'_V$ lie over the same base map and have the same composite to $z'$, so lifting uniqueness makes them equal. Applying $F$ proves restriction compatibility. Semilinearity gives $F(a_V)(rs)=\operatorname{pr}_V^*(r)F(a_V)(s)$, exactly the $\mathcal O_{U'}(V)$-linearity required for $d_{a,F}:R_{z'}F\to u_*R_zF$. Naturality of a module morphism $F\to G$ on $a_V$ gives naturality of $d$ in $F$.

source.place: Construction equation-comparison-push before Tag 075D, and equation-comparison-modules after Tag 06W9

proof.text: Define $c_{a,F}$ to be the adjoint of $d_{a,F}$ under [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction]. Its naturality in $F$ follows by applying the natural Hom bijection to the equality of $d$-squares just proved. For $a=\mathrm{id}_z$, the arrow $a_V$ is the identity after identifying the chosen lifts, so $d_{a,F}$ is the identity. The identity pullback is canonically the identity functor by uniqueness of left adjoints [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation]; its unit is the identity, so its adjoint $c_{a,F}$ is the identity as claimed.

source.place: Tag 075D, naturality and identity verification omitted in source; module extension following equation-comparison-modules

proof.text: For $a:z\to z'$ over $u:U\to U'$ and $b:z'\to z''$ over $v:U'\to U''$, the projection-preserving isomorphism $U\times_{U'}(U'\times_{U''}W)\cong U\times_{U''}W$ of [def-pc-fibre-product] identifies $(vu)_*$ with $v_*u_*$, including their scalar maps (successive pullback of regular functions is composite pullback). Under this identification the unique lifted arrow for $ba$ is $b_W\circ a_{B_vW}$ by lifting uniqueness. Contravariance gives $d_{ba,F}=v_*(d_{a,F})\circ d_{b,F}$. By [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction], transposing through $u^*v^*\dashv v_*u_*$ means first transposing through $u^*\dashv u_*$ and then through $v^*\dashv v_*$. The transpose of $c_{a,F}\circ u^*(c_{b,F})$ is therefore $v_*(d_{a,F})\circ d_{b,F}$, precisely $d_{ba,F}$. The canonical isomorphism $(vu)^*\cong u^*v^*$ is the unique unit-compatible one for these right adjoints, by [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation]. Equality under the bijective Hom correspondence proves the stated composition law for these actual maps.

source.place: Tag 075D(1), module extension following equation-comparison-modules; sites-modules.tex composition lemma after Tag 03D7

proof.text: Suppose $u$ is etale. Postcomposition $I_u:U_{\mathrm{et}}\to U'_{\mathrm{et}}$ identifies $U_{\mathrm{et}}$ with $U'_{\mathrm{et}}/U$: a scheme etale over $U$ is etale over $U'$ by composition, and a factorization $W\to U\to U'$ with $W,U$ etale over $U'$ has $W\to U$ etale by cancellation [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. These mutually inverse assignments act identically on arrows and coverings. Precomposition $I_u^s$ sends sheaves to sheaves, since a cover and its pairwise intersections are literally the same schemes on the two sites. The functor $B_u$ also preserves sheaves by Step 3. The adjunction $I_u\dashv B_u$ and its projection counit are supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-localization-functor-adjoint]; hence [lem-weil-pbc-sets-adjoint-continuous-restriction-adjunction] identifies $u^{-1}$ with $I_u^s$, with unit at $V$ the restriction along $B_uV\to V$. On rings this identifies $u^{-1}\mathcal O_{U'}$ with $\mathcal O_U$ by the identity on $\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_W)$; the structural map is this identity since its adjunct is the projection pullback. Thus $u^*$ is also slice restriction on modules: $\mathcal O_U\otimes_{\mathcal O_U}I_u^sM\cong I_u^sM$, by $r\otimes m\mapsto rm$ with inverse $m\mapsto1\otimes m$.

source.place: Tag 075D(2); ringed restriction Tag 06W9; topologies.tex Tag 021I and descent.tex Tag 070R

proof.text: Still with $u$ etale, for $W\to U$ etale the object $z_W$ is canonically isomorphic to the lift $z'_{W\to U'}$: both map cartesianly to $z'$ over $W\to U'$. Denote the resulting sectionwise isomorphism $e:I_u^sR_{z'}F\to R_zF$. The uniqueness of lifts makes it commute with all restrictions. Its adjunct at $V\to U'$ is restriction from $F(z'_V)$ to the lift over $B_uV$, followed by $e$ there, because the unit in Step 7 is projection restriction. This composite is $F(a_V)$, since the corresponding composite arrow is the unique $a_V$ from Step 4. Thus its adjunct is $d_{a,F}$, and the injective Hom bijection of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction] identifies $e$ with $c_{a,F}$. Hence the specified comparison is an isomorphism, not merely some unspecified isomorphism of its source and target.

source.place: Tag 075D(2), verification of the specific comparison in equation-comparison-modules

proof.text: A functor $h:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$ over schemes preserves cartesian arrows: the unique factorization characterization in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids] holds for every arrow of a fibred groupoid. Use [lem-sfb-fibred-site-functor-continuity] with base the big etale scheme site. It applies to the chosen small models and proves that precomposition sends sheaves of sets to sheaves of sets. On the underlying abelian sheaf $h^*F$ the addition and zero are the original ones; its scalar ring at $y$ over $T$ is $\mathcal O_{\mathcal C}(h(y))=\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)=\mathcal O_{\mathcal D}(y)$. The module laws and semilinearity on arrows are consequently exactly those of $F$, proving that this is a module sheaf. This uses no comparison between fppf and etale sheaf categories.

source.place: Tag 06TS and Tag 06WE, etale version explicitly stated after its tensor formula

proof.text: For $y$ over $U$ and $V\to U$ etale, $h(y_V)\to h(y)$ and the chosen lift $(h(y))_V\to h(y)$ are uniquely isomorphic over $V$. Applying $F$ gives $F(h(y_V))\cong F((h(y))_V)$, hence $R_y(h^*F)\cong R_{h(y)}F$. For $a:y\to y'$ the image under $h$ of the lifted arrow $a_V$ of Step 4 is the unique arrow used for $h(a)$: its base map and its composite to $h(y')$ are the prescribed ones. The sectionwise isomorphisms therefore carry $d_{a,h^*F}$ to $d_{h(a),F}$. They are linear since all maps of scalar rings along the isomorphisms over $V$ are identities. Naturality of the same module Hom bijection carries their adjoints $c_{a,h^*F}$ to $c_{h(a),F}$. Identity arrows, empty schemes and the zero module satisfy the identical formulas; nowhere was a quasi-coherence, flatness, representability or algebraicity hypothesis introduced.
